newsitem.title: CHINA: HK police arrest 22 suspected Vietnamese boatpeople.
newsitem.headline: HK police arrest 22 suspected Vietnamese boatpeople.

text.p: Hong Kong police have arrested 22 suspected illegal Vietnamese immigrants after a massive manhunt prompted by reports that hundreds had jumped ship in the territory, police said on Tuesday.
Police said they captured four boatpeople early on Tuesday after detaining 18 on Monday on the rural outlying island of Lantau.
Those detained told police they had been dropped off by a freighter on Sunday and claimed 600 immigrants were on board.
But police called off the land, sea and air search after they suspected the claims were bogus, said Lantau deputy district commander Steve Caruthers.

"Some of them have admitted they have been in Chek Lap Kok for a few days prior to their arrest," Caruthers said. "They couldn't find work. They met with other Vietnamese who arrived separately. They then tried to head to the urban areas."
Hong Kong is building a US$9.1 billion new international airport at Chek Lap Kok adjoining Lantau.
The latest batch of boatpeople left Quang Ninh in northern Vietnam 12 days ago, Hong Kong television said.
In recent years, Hong Kong has been repatriating tens of thousands of illegal Vietnamese migrants who were not recognised as genuine refugees.
Repatriation became more frequent in the months approaching Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1. Beijing demanded all detention camps be cleared by the handover.
But some 3,000 Vietnamese are still in the territory, the remnants of a human flood who left Vietnam after the communists won the war there in 1975.
